messages:
sam (Customer): Hey team — started getting 429s around 08:12 UTC. Happens in short bursts, then clears. Body says "rate limit exceeded". We use a single API key across many clients behind our NAT. Request-id in response: rid_7b9f.

maria (Support): Sorry for the trouble. Can you paste the full response headers from one failed request? Also are you going through a proxy/load balancer that might collapse client IPs?

sam (Customer): Yup using a managed proxy (connects from a pool of egress IPs). Example headers we saw: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 25
x-request-id: rid_7b9f
content-type: application/json
```
We also send the API key in Authorization: Bearer sk-live-abc.

maria (Support): Thanks. That header set points to a per-IP/egress quota being hit (limit 120). We have multiple quota dimensions: org, project, API key, and IP. Our routing tries to apply the most specific applicable quota. Because your traffic originates from a small set of shared IPs, your aggregate across keys likely exhausted the IP quota.

sam (Customer): Hmm — is there a way to confirm which quota blocked the request? The error body didn't say dimension. We rely on the key for billing, so org/project quotas shouldn't matter.

maria (Support): We can confirm on our side. Quick troubleshooting steps:
1) Share a failed response (headers + x-request-id) — we can look up enforcement reason.
2) Try a request directly from a client IP (bypass proxy) to see if key-based quota still triggers.
3) If you can, set X-Forwarded-For to the original client IP to avoid NAT collapse (only if your proxy preserves it).

sam (Customer): Sending two rids: rid_7b9f and rid_7c01. Also share a curl cmd we used:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-abc" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
We can test adding X-Forwarded-For, but not all clients set it.

maria (Support): Got the rids. @jordan (SRE) can you check enforcement logs for those request ids and confirm dimension flagged?

jordan (SRE): Looking now — enforcement entries show "quota_exceeded: dimension=egress_ip, value=198.51.100.23" for both rids. Limit for that IP pool is 120 rps (rolling window) given your plan + burst settings. The calls from that IP aggregated across multiple org keys.

sam (Customer): So even though we have a unique API key per customer instance, the IP quota is shared and that's the blocker? Can we get per-key enforcement instead?

jordan (SRE): Correct — there are multiple quota layers. Enforcement chooses the first violated layer in this order: API key -> project -> org -> egress IP -> global. We try to report the dimension in logs, but the client-facing body is minimized to avoid leaking policy details. We can change support UX to surface dimension in certain cases.

sam (Customer): Short-term how do we stop the 429s? Long-term preferred fix?

maria (Support): Short-term options:
- Configure your proxy to forward X-Forwarded-For so our gateway can attribute requests to originating clients (reduces NAT-surfacing).
- Rotate to use more egress IPs / larger NAT pool to spread the load.
- Request a temporary increase on the egress_ip quota while you re-architect.

Long-term: we recommend per-key rate limits for business-critical tenants (Reserved capacity or Dedicated), or move to a per-key enforcement mode for your account so each API key has isolated quotas rather than shared by IP.

sam (Customer): We'll try X-Forwarded-For test. Also would like a temporary bump. What's the process?

maria (Support): @lee (Billing) can approve a temporary egress quota bump for this org while we validate. We'll need expected RPS and duration. Also need to confirm there's no unintended billing spike.

lee (Billing): I can approve a 2x burst for 48 hours pending risk review. Please provide expected sustained RPS and whether clients are on shared/free tiers. I'll log the change and notify if usage approaches the cap.

sam (Customer): Expected peak RPS 220 for ~2 hours, then back to ~60. Clients on pay tier.

maria (Support): Approved: we'll open a temporary quota ticket and enable a 48-hour egress_ip bump to 240 for IP 198.51.100.23. Also we'll add a note to return to baseline.

jordan (SRE): Follow-ups for us:
- Add diagnostic to surface enforcement dimension in support lookups.
- Add a heuristic to warn customers when many API keys share <N> egress IPs.
- Consider offering per-key egress isolation as a product option.

sam (Customer): Thanks — will test X-Forwarded-For. Quick question: if we set X-Forwarded-For to the real client IP, can you always trust it? Some CDNs allow custom sets so we need trust chain.

jordan (SRE): We only honor X-Forwarded-For from our verified proxies (we check the source IP matches an allowed proxy). If your proxy is in our allowed list we will parse it; otherwise we ignore it to prevent spoofing.

sam (Customer): Great. I set X-Forwarded-For for a test request and the 429s stopped for that client. Confirmed.

maria (Support): Awesome. I'll keep the temporary bump active while you roll out proxy changes. I'll close the ticket in 48 hours unless you ask us to extend. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: quota-ticket #QT-2891 created -> egress_ip bump 198.51.100.23 to 240 for 48h (requested by maria).

sam (Customer): Appreciate the quick help. Please keep us posted if you change enforcement behavior.

maria (Support): Will do. Logging action items and follow-ups in the ticket: 1) diagnostic surface, 2) heuristic warning, 3) product per-key isolation exploration.

jordan (SRE): Closing loop — enforcement logs, diagnostic entries, and temporary quota change documented in QT-2891. Reach out if any new rids appear.

sam (Customer): Closing from our side — no 429s after proxy update. Thanks all!
